title: Gradual rollouts: canary + A/B primer (wip)
content:
Status: WIP - high-level primer and working checklist for cross-functional gradual rollouts, canaries, and A/B tests in Redwood Console.

Purpose:
- Provide a concise operational checklist and decision matrix for product, engineering, SRE, and sales/support to run safe gradual rollouts.
- Capture minimum observability, metrics, and rollback conditions so teams can do fast, repeatable experiments with low blast radius.

When to use this doc (non-exhaustive):
- New model / model variant deployed to hosted API or Dedicated pools.
- Changes to routing policies (e.g., latency vs cost preference, region routing).
- Console feature changes that alter request shaping (batching, caching toggles).
- UX changes that depend on model output quality (templated system prompts, function-calling schemas).

Quick definitions (as used here):
- Canary: small percentage of live traffic routed to new variant to validate basic safety / infra correctness. Short duration, focused on safety signals.
- A/B: controlled experiment comparing two or more variants with target metrics and statistical analysis. Longer durations, powered for significance.
- Ramp: staged increase in traffic to a variant after passing defined checks.

Roles & responsibilities (short):
- Product: defines hypothesis, primary/secondary metrics, user segments, rollout percentage schedule.
- Eng (serving/runtime): implements routing config, ensures model variant compatibility, prepares fallback routes.
- Observability / SRE: builds quick dashboards, sets alerts, runs smoke tests.
- Solutions / CS: identifies any high-value customer cohorts to exclude or target.
- Legal / Trust if output-affecting changes require review.

Canary cookbook (practical checklist):
1) Pre-deploy checks (pre-cut):
   - Confirm model artifact, checksum, and start-up logs pass smoke.
   - Unit integration tests for any new function calling or structured outputs.
   - Capacity check: ensure Dedicated pool or hosted region can absorb spike.
2) Configure canary route:
   - Start with 0.1% or a small fixed cohort (0.5% for low-risk infra-only changes).
   - Keep canary duration short (30–120 min) for infra changes, 1–48h for output/quality changes.
3) Observability to enable before traffic:
   - Latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, timeouts, HTTP 5xx, inference runtime OOMs.
   - Token-level cost delta and per-request cost distribution.
   - Quality regression smoke: run a 100-case prompt suite (kept in repo) and compare top-k metrics (pass/fail).
   - Output distribution checks: response lengths, tokenization anomalies, hallucination heuristics (where available).
4) Acceptance criteria for canary (example):
   - p95 latency increase < 10% vs baseline AND absolute p95 < SLO threshold.
   - Error rate increase < 0.1% (or relative <10% of baseline).
   - Cost per token not > +20% without prior approval.
   - Eval harness: no >5% regression on smoke prompt set (define metric: accuracy/f1/baseline score).
5) Auto-rollback triggers:
   - If any hard signal crosses high-severity threshold (e.g., sustained 5xx > 1% for 5m) then immediate fallback to prior variant.
   - If quality smoke fails above tolerance for 3 consecutive runs.

Ramp schedule examples (tunable):
- Infra-only changes: 0.1% -> 1% (30m) -> 5% (1h) -> 20% (2h) -> 100% (gradual over day).
- Model outputs / prompt changes: 0.5% -> 2% (4h) -> 10% (24h) -> 50% (48h) -> 100% (after manual review).
- For customer-targeted experiments, start with seeded cohorts (internal + canary customers) before broad traffic.

A/B experiment primer (concise):
- Hypothesis: short sentence (e.g., "Prompt v2 reduces hallucination on product-detail prompts and reduces average follow-up messages").
- Primary metric: single metric to power for (e.g., reduction in follow-up prompt rate, conversion, model-score delta).
- Secondary metrics: latency, cost, errors, NPS/qual surveys for human-facing changes.
- Sample sizing: rough calc placeholder (use team analytics): target delta, baseline conversion, alpha=0.05, power=0.8.
- Exposure and blocking: ensure deterministic routing for repeatable sessions (sticky assignment for session-level experiments).
- Instrumentation: log variant-id, model-version, prompt-template-id, user-cohort, response tokens, any function calls.
- Minimum run time rule: reach min sample AND observe at least one full business cycle (24–72h depending on traffic).

Observability and dashboard checklist (fast deploy):
- Quick dashboard: canary vs baseline time series for latency p50/p95/p99, errors, cost-per-request, token distribution.
- Health alerts: p95 > SLO, error rate jump > X, OOMs or GPU OOMs, queue depth.
- Quality alert: automated eval harness failure rate > tolerance.
- Tracing: capture request traces including model variant, kernel selection, batching wait time.
- Log retention note: keep canary logs for at least X days (team decision).

Data and analysis notes:
- Collect per-request and per-token metadata; avoid PII in logs. Anonymize or hash user ids.
- Post-hoc slice checks: by region, customer tier, length buckets, prompt types.
- Prefer uplift-style reporting for A/B (treatment lift, confidence intervals). Use Bayesian approach for low-sample experiments if appropriate.

Rollout decision matrix (simplified):
- If infra signals fail -> immediate rollback.
- If cost increases but quality improves -> require product + finance sign-off for rollout.
- If quality regresses on key slices -> stop, triage with model/ML teams, consider controlled rollback to subset.

Console / platform integration hooks (items to product/eng for Console):
- Expose canary config templating: percent, cohorts (email lists, user segments), automatic ramp scheduler.
- Provide one-click rollback and fallback to a compatible model variant (fallback policy hints).
- Surface per-route cost delta and token breakdown during rollout in the Console.
- Auto-run smoke-eval on deploy and annotate rollout records with eval results.

Operational runbook (short):
- On alert, page on-call SRE + owning eng. Product PM joins within 30m.
- Triage: check dashboard, compare baseline traffic, inspect recent deploys and infra changes.
- If rollback condition met -> execute rollback, notify stakeholders, open postmortem ticket.

Open questions / TODOs (actionable items):
- [ ] Standardize a 100-prompt smoke suite per model family, stored in repo and runnable by CI. Owner: Eng-ML.
- [ ] Decide default canary durations for hosting vs Dedicated. Owner: SRE/Product.
- [ ] Implement Console annotation for "eval harness result" on rollout timeline. Owner: Console team.
- [ ] Flesh out statistical analysis runbook for non-stats teams (analytics cookbook). Owner: Product-Analytics.
- [ ] Policy for experiments that touch regulated PII workflows (Legal review gating). Owner: Trust & Legal.

Notes to self / shorthand (will expand into formal runbook later):
- Keep conservative defaults: smaller cohorts, longer observation for semantic changes.
- Use combination of automated and human checks for quality. Auto-rollback for infra; manual rollback for nuanced quality regressions.
- Track cost delta closely — sometimes cheaper model configurations are tempting but introduce reliability risks.

References / links:
- Console rollout pages (TODO link)
- JIRA tickets: JIRA-3456 (rollout infra), JIRA-3567 (eval harness infra)
- GH: rollouts repo PR #98 for routing policy changes

If you’re reading this and want to run something tomorrow: ping in #prod-rollouts with the below template:
- Short hypothesis (1 line)
- Primary metric and expected direction
- Recommended canary schedule (percent + duration)
- Owner + on-call contacts
- Preconditions met (smoke suite run? dashboards ready?)

End of primer (WIP).
